metadata.title: Evolution Of Post-Impact Remnant Helium Stars In Type Ia Supernova Remnants Within The Single-Degenerate Scenario

evidence.quote: HVSs have extremely high space motions and can be unbound in our Galaxy; for example, US 708 has v \sin i = 708 \pm 15 \text{ km s}^{-1} (Hirsch et al. 2005).

The HVS US 708 (or HVS2) has a radial velocity v\sin i = 708\pm 15\mathrm{km~s}^{-1}, T_{\mathrm{eff}} = 44, 500\mathrm{K}, \log g = 5.23, and Galactic latitude b = +47.05^{\circ} at a distance of 19\mathrm{kpc} (Hirsch et al. 2005), giving a displacement of 14\mathrm{kpc} from the Galactic plane.
HVSs have extremely high space motions and can be unbound in our Galaxy; for example, US 708 has v \sin i = 708 \pm 15 \text{ km s}^{-1} (Hirsch et al. 2005).

The effective temperature and surface gravity of US 708 are consistent with our He PIRS models, but they require a subdwarf lifetime longer than several times 10^{7} yr to reach such a distance, if the SN exploded in the Galactic plane. Therefore, a less massive model may better match US 708, since less massive models have higher linear speeds and longer subdwarf lifetimes.

values.condition: Reported for US 708 (HVS2) as a radial velocity; the paper writes this as v sin i.

evidence.quote: The HVS US 708 (or HVS2) has a radial velocity v\sin i = 708\pm 15\mathrm{km~s}^{-1}

notes: US 708 is included as follow_up: T:p6-b1 links it to HVSs that can be unbound and cites Hirsch et al. (2005), while T:p29-b2 analyzes whether the He PIRS models can match it. The simulated post-impact remnants are not individually established as Galactic-unbound candidates, so they are not listed.

US 708: US 708 and HVS2 are identified as the same star in T:p29-b2. The paper explicitly calls the 708 ± 15 km s−1 value a radial velocity, although it writes it using the symbol v sin i, which conventionally denotes projected rotational velocity; the value is retained as the reported radial velocity. The quoted 14 kpc is a displacement from the Galactic plane, not a galactocentric radius, so it is not recorded as galactocentric_radius.
